input.quote: Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:
input.rationale: The Base Agreement runs for an initial three-year term (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause - material breach, insolvency, competitor acquisition, or continuing force majeure (p0107 to p0118). No convenience exit exists for IBM anywhere: Section 4.0's six-month notice is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL, not T4C) and SOW Section 6.1 reaches individual Purchase Orders only, subject to cost reimbursement. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is a missing-behaviour deviation, so we insert operative language: 'IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL', with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The narrow 'Notwithstanding Section 5.1' opener prevents MSL from reading the retained for-cause preamble as exclusive, without deleting or rewriting Section 5.1. Direction is checked: MSL has no mid-term convenience right because Section 5.1 confines termination by either Party to cause, so preferred element 4 is already met and no new restriction on MSL is drafted. Placement inside Section 5.0 preserves Section 4.0's cross-reference, and Sections 5.2, 5.3 and SOW 6.1 survive unchanged. 60 to 90 days' notice remains the fallback concession.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 5.4: IBM convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, prevailing over the Section 5.1 for-cause preamble
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5.0 today allows exit only for cause, leaving us locked into a three-year term, so we have added Section 5.4 under which IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience on thirty (30) days' prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" opener keeps the for-cause rights intact while ensuring that preamble is not read as an exclusive list; we can move to 60-90 days' notice as our fallback.

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience by IBM. Notwithstanding Section 5.1, IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
